workflow.title: Review developer build folders before cleaning a Mac
workflow.primaryIntent: Distinguish disposable generated output from committed project data, environments and cloud-only files before approving cleanup.
workflow.angle: Use DeepCleanMac 1.7.0/1.7.1 Git-aware exclusions and 1.6.7 counting fix as concrete documented reasons not to treat a scan total as permission to delete.
sections: Start with a keep/rebuild/unknown decision, not a cleanup target.
Separate committed project content, regenerable output and environment state.
Explain the dated vendor protection changes without pretending to test them.
Review exact location, permissions, rebuild cost and backup before approval.
Show Breathing Room, which we build, as an optional review/investigation preview, not a replacement for every suite tool.
visualPlan: Cleared DeepCleanMac app UI required; current link-only dashboard is not enough.
Selected current-source Space preview, example data banners and caption intact.
workflow.interactionHandoff: A non-destructive decision checklist: committed/unknown → keep; generated → confirm reproducible rebuild, owner and exact location before review. No shell deletion demo, scan, upload or invented saved-byte calculator.
workflow.limitations: No SERP-volume evidence collected; title uniqueness across future drafts needs independent review; no hands-on claims.

comparison.boundedConclusion: DeepCleanMac may fit someone needing the documented updater/uninstaller/duplicate tools. Breathing Room, which we build, may fit someone willing to use a non-notarized Python-dependent preview for source-backed investigation and exact approval workflows. Neither was benchmarked here.
